question: According to the unit, why does rewriting an authentic text to lower its difficulty undermine its value?
options: It makes the text too short to support a full lesson activity
It removes culturally appropriate idiomatic language
It prevents teachers from using the material across multiple proficiency levels
It increases the cultural load by introducing unfamiliar simplified vocabulary
answer: It removes culturally appropriate idiomatic language
anchor: A simplified advertisement no longer reflects real use of language in culturally appropriate contexts

question: The unit describes the tourist album project about the Sinai Peninsula as an example of authentic materials supporting which specific outcome beyond the classroom?
options: Students submitted their work to an international language competition
The library received the album, creating an audience beyond the class
Older students presented the album to a local tourism board
The album was published on the internet for other language learners
answer: The library received the album, creating an audience beyond the class
anchor: The finished album was added to the school library, giving the project an audience beyond the classroom

question: Which of the following best explains why a student who follows local football will tolerate more linguistic difficulty in a match report than in an article about an unfamiliar sport?
options: Football vocabulary is simpler and contains fewer technical terms than other sports
The student brings prior knowledge to the text and compensates for gaps in linguistic understanding
Match reports are always written at a lower reading level than other newspaper articles
The teacher has pre-taught the key vocabulary before the student reads the report
answer: The student brings prior knowledge to the text and compensates for gaps in linguistic understanding
anchor: students bring prior knowledge to the text and compensate for gaps in linguistic understanding

question: The unit identifies a fifth reason authentic materials motivate learners that is distinct from interest, cultural relevance, personal connection, and survival skills. What is that fifth reason, and what does it train learners to do?
answer: The fifth reason is that authentic materials train learners to extract meaning from language they do not fully understand, developing tolerance for partial comprehension — a skill no controlled exercise can replicate.
anchor: authentic materials train learners to extract meaning from language they do not fully understand
